messages.content:
# Kestrel Point (KP-1871)

Registry of Coastal Lights, northern district

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Registry ID | KP-1871 |
| Location | Northern headland, Marrow Bay |
| Coordinates | 55.912 N, 4.381 W |
| Tower | Cast iron, painted white with one red band |
| Tower height | 18 m |
| Focal height | 34 m above mean high water |
| Light character | Fl(2) W 10s |
| Range | 17 nautical miles |
| Status | Active (automated) |

## History

Construction of the tower began in the spring of 1869 after two wrecks on the
Marrow Shoal in the winter of 1867. The ironwork was cast inland and shipped
in sections; the lantern and a second-order lens arrived in the summer of 1871.

The light was first lit on 3 November 1871.

The station originally had a principal keeper and one assistant. The first
principal keeper was A. Moreau, who had previously served as assistant at
Grey Gull Rock. The assistant post was filled by a series of short-term
appointments until 1876.

A fog signal building was added in 1894. The original oil lamp was replaced
by a paraffin vapor burner in 1912 and the light was electrified in 1951.

The station was automated in 1986 and the keepers' cottages were sold. The
tower is maintained by the district lighthouse authority.

## Keepers

| Years | Principal keeper |
|---|---|
| 1871-1889 | A. Moreau |
| 1889-1903 | T. Lindqvist |
| 1903-1921 | R. Okafor |
| 1921-1950 | various |
| 1950-1986 | see station records |

## Sources

1. District lighthouse authority annual returns, 1870-1875.
2. Marrow Bay harbor board minutes, vol. 4.
3. Station logbooks (digitized 2019).

Last reviewed: 2024-02-11
